title: feat(query): accept the SHA256 fingerprint git prints
description: When git verify-tag fails it prints only 'Good "git" signature with ED25519 key SHA256:<fp>' and 'No principal matched.', the same for an unregistered key and a below-tier key (measured for vouch-tq92.5, git 2.55.0 / OpenSSH 9.6p1). Today 'git vouch query SHA256:<fp>' prints handle null and exits 1 even for a registered contributor, and does not reject the input as not a did:key. 'git vouch did SHA256:<fp>' errors with 'not an SSH public key line'. So neither Linus nor the sender can tell 'contributor' from 'not registered' without the public key. Proposal: make query (and query --at) match a SHA256 fingerprint against the person files' keys, and reject input that is neither a did:key nor a fingerprint. Then 'git vouch query SHA256:<fp>' answers handle, tier and added time with no new command; compare tiers to tell it apart from the export's --min-tier. A constraint on input rather than a new 'git vouch why' command. Once it lands, update guide-anchors 'Switch Linus's git' to name it. Not built.
close_reason: Won't do: not requested; the documented floor and existing query input cover it
